conventions.convention: The finite graph has N≥1 transitions indexed 0 through N−1, permits varying state dimensions, and differentiates its actual C1 maps in exact real arithmetic.
Gradients are columns; vector norms are Euclidean and matrix norms are induced operator norms.
At T=0 the parameter-flow assertion concerns initial evaluation only and asserts no time derivative on a singleton. The continuous adjoint and pairing formulas require T>0.
Elliptic forms are real bilinear forms, need not be symmetric, and the adjoint equation is aθ(v,p)=DuJ[v]. Parameter data are C1 in operator norm with uniform neighborhood coercivity.
The weighted gradient-error branch requires nonnegative weights summing to T. The independent local-C1 consistency branch permits negative or zero RK weights.
Implicit sensitivities differentiate the selected exact algebraic stage branch with nonsingular residual Jacobian.
Parabolic states use a real evolution triple, T>0, weak time derivatives in W(0,T;V), and continuous H traces. The definition specifies bilinear forms without imposing their boundedness.
Time-dependent comparison maps are C1 in operator norm; their residual derivative includes P′u+Pu′−u′. Adjoint reversal changes the sign of the projection time derivative.
QR factors have positive real diagonals, n,N≥1, and log-volume means log|det(A_N⋯A_1)| over a finite horizon.

load_bearing.statement: For the finite C1 state-step objective, S₀=Dx₀ and Sₙ₊₁=AₙSₙ+Bₙ; p_N=Dxφᵀ and pₙ=Dxℓₙᵀ+Aₙᵀpₙ₊₁. Its exact gradient is Dθφᵀ+S₀ᵀp₀+Σₙ(Dθℓₙᵀ+Bₙᵀpₙ₊₁).

Under the stated C1 field, C1 initial map, unique positive-horizon solutions and bounded convex common tube with compact closure in the open domain, θ↦uθ is C1 into C([0,T];Rᵈ). For T>0 its derivative uniquely solves S′=f_uS+f_θ, S(0)=Du₀; T=0 has the separate initial-evaluation conclusion.

Under its uniform local value and first-derivative consistency, derivative stability and size, exact-derivative Lipschitz, initial-data, terminal-derivative and tube hypotheses, the state, actual graph tangent, nodal adjoint and reduced gradient have the displayed order-p bounds with constants X,C_S,C_P,C_G.

For the actual explicit RK state and matching cost maps, the stated C2 base-data, common-tube and local augmented-order hypotheses supply the preceding lemma's local consistency, stability, derivative-size and derivative-Lipschitz hypotheses. The stated augmented C4 condition and coefficient equations instantiate orders through four.

Assuming Countable Choice, uniform neighborhood coercivity and operator-norm C1 data, each elliptic state exists uniquely and depends C1 on θ; its derivative satisfies aθ(wη,v)=Dθℓθ[η](v)−Dθaθ[η](uθ,v).
Assuming Countable Choice and the stated differentiable coercive state setting, the transposed adjoint gives Dj(θ)[η]=DθJ(uθ,θ)[η]+Dθℓθ[η](pθ)−Dθaθ[η](uθ,pθ). No symmetry is required.
Under the stated differentiable state, linearized equation, objective differentiation and terminal adjoint hypotheses, Dj[η]=Dθφ[η]+(p(0),u₀′[η])_H+∫₀ᵀ(DθL[η]+⟨fθ′[η],p⟩−aθ′[η](uθ,p))dt.

For invertible real square factors and positive-diagonal QR updates A_kQ_{k−1}=Q_kR_k, log|det(A_N⋯A_1)|=Σ_{k,i}log r_{k,ii}. The numerical log bound additionally requires the stated positive singular-value floor and certified diagonal/log errors.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.2 uses 'the adjoint equation with v=w_η and the linearized state equation with v=p', although the Statement gives equations 'for every v∈V and almost every t'. Neither this theorem nor def-parameterized-parabolic-variational-problem requires the bilinear forms to be bounded, so fixed-test equations cannot in general be substituted at time-dependent tests. Under the written fixed-test quantifier order the claim is false. A counterexample in ZFC: take T=1 and V=H=ℓ²(R), with w(t)=(1,t,t²/2!,t³/3!,...). The vectors w(t), 0≤t≤1, are linearly independent by the finite Vandermonde determinant. Extend them to a Hamel basis and let λ_t be the coefficient functional of w(t). For each fixed v, λ_t(v) is nonzero at only finitely many times. Set aθ(t;x,y)=λ_t(x)(e₀,y), independently of θ; uθ(t)=θw(t); fθ(t)=θ(w′(t)+e₀); u₀,θ=θe₀; L=0; and φ(x,θ)=(e₀,x). The state and tangent equations hold for all tests at every time. The constant p=e₀ satisfies the written adjoint equation for every fixed test almost everywhere, since λ_t(v)=0 almost everywhere, and has the required terminal value. All state, forcing, objective and parameter derivatives have the required regularity. The true reduced objective is j(θ)=θ, whereas the asserted formula gives Dj[1]=1+∫₀¹(e₀,w′+e₀)dt=2. An explicit bounded-form/operator-equation hypothesis, or appropriately strengthened simultaneous-test assumptions, is needed to license the cancellation.
